pain_point: Advisors often need multiple disconnected systems to reconstruct a student's current situation
affected_role: Advisors faculty support staff and students
severity_rationale: Fragmented context delays help creates duplicate records and forces students to repeat their stories
evidence_type: sector guide and institutional/vendor case evidence
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2026 and current. EDUCAUSE says disconnected systems leave advisors toggling and students falling through gaps; TCU described noncentral notes and repeated student stories before consolidation
prevalence_limitations: EDUCAUSE is a sector synthesis; TCU evidence is vendor-published and institution-specific

pain_point: Early alerts without a named owner action and closure state become an alert queue rather than support
severity_rationale: Unowned alerts can leave urgent needs unresolved while creating the appearance that the institution acted
evidence_type: vendor workflow guidance and sector evidence
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): current. Stellic's early-alert guidance explicitly says each flag needs an owner action and recorded outcome; EDUCAUSE emphasizes meaningful exchange and action rather than data movement alone
prevalence_limitations: Stellic source is vendor-authored; failure frequency is not quantified

pain_point: Degree-audit output can look authoritative even when program coding transfer credit exceptions or refresh timing make it incomplete
affected_role: Students advisors registrars and graduation auditors
severity_rationale: A mistaken interpretation can lead to unnecessary courses missed requirements delayed graduation or aid issues
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): current. Terra State says Degree Works uses best fit that may not be perfect depends on Banner data and nightly refresh and does not replace an advisor; Maryland says uAchieve does not imply degree clearance
prevalence_limitations: Two institution examples across different products; local rules and processes vary

pain_point: Complex program requirements and incorrect SIS coding can overwhelm a degree-audit implementation and compress validation time
affected_role: Registrar academic programs IT and advisors
severity_rationale: Incorrect audits undermine trust and can affect graduation decisions across many programs
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2026. Johns Hopkins reports significant delay from program complexity and incorrect SIS configuration and changed to phased sprints
prevalence_limitations: One university's implementation; does not measure typical Stellic implementation performance

pain_point: Advisor role and privilege management may require institution-built tooling
severity_rationale: Local privilege work adds maintenance risk around sensitive notes and student records
source_context: Verified incentivized Capterra review by an IT director says the institution had to build advisor role/privilege management itself
prevalence_limitations: Single review from one configuration and older version

pain_point: Staff report multi-click navigation and limited personalization of templates
severity_rationale: Small interaction costs compound across large caseloads and can reduce adoption
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2019-2025. G2 reviewers describe clicking through many options toggling between screens and limited template customization
prevalence_limitations: Eleven-review convenience sample across years and versions; no prevalence estimate

pain_point: Risk scores can replicate bias or change staff expectations when data definitions model behavior and fairness are opaque
affected_role: Students advisors institutional research and governance
severity_rationale: A false or biased label can alter who receives attention and how staff perceive a student
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2018-2022. Advising Success Network calls for addressing AI/ML bias privacy and student knowledge/control; EDUCAUSE asks whether profiles bias expectations and behavior
prevalence_limitations: Guidance identifies risk mechanisms; it does not establish harm prevalence for a named vendor

pain_point: Negative or vague alerts can discourage students when they do not include a concrete supportive next step
severity_rationale: An alert can increase anxiety or disengagement if it communicates judgment without useful action
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2020. EDUCAUSE found most reported nudges focused on shortcomings and recommends positive messages plus specific actions and resources
prevalence_limitations: 2020 survey is older and describes student-reported alerts generally rather than one platform

pain_point: Students may not know that advising early-alert or resource tools exist even after institutional deployment
severity_rationale: A technically available service creates no benefit when students cannot find or understand it
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2020. EDUCAUSE reports substantial disagreement among students at the same institutions about whether success tools were available
prevalence_limitations: Older sector survey; availability awareness may have changed

pain_point: Inconsistent note systems and permissions fragment the student's support history and create privacy risk
affected_role: Advisors counselors student affairs and IT
severity_rationale: Over-sharing exposes sensitive records while under-sharing causes repeated intake and missed context
evidence_type: sector guide and vendor technical documentation
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): current. Advising Success Network describes noninterfacing note systems; Civitas documentation exposes institution-configured private/shared notes and unit-level visibility as necessary controls
prevalence_limitations: The sources establish the design problem but not a comparative incidence rate

pain_point: Faculty adoption and timely data entry determine whether early alerts arrive soon enough to act
severity_rationale: Late incomplete signals make predictive or routing features operationally irrelevant
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): 2012-2022. EDUCAUSE documents labor-intensive late alerts; Advising Success Network emphasizes stakeholder roles and implementation adoption
prevalence_limitations: The evidence spans institutions and years but does not quantify current cross-sector response rates

pain_point: Custom point-to-point integrations create stale duplicate or semantically inconsistent student data
affected_role: IT data governance advisors and students
severity_rationale: Bad integration can amplify inconsistent definitions at scale and direct staff to the wrong intervention
source_context: EDUCAUSE identifies manual transfer duplicated data unclear flows and mismatched definitions as core interoperability failures
prevalence_limitations: Sector guidance is not a measured vendor comparison

pain_point: Implementation success depends on cross-functional governance and change champions beyond the software team
affected_role: Advising leaders faculty IT registrars and students
severity_rationale: Poor ownership can leave workflows unstaffed permissions unresolved and features unused
source_context: Advising Success Network synthesizes 12 institutions and identifies multiple stakeholder roles; it also notes students were often absent from implementation decisions
prevalence_limitations: Qualitative case synthesis; successful examples may underrepresent failed implementations

pain_point: Predictive prioritization cannot create advising capacity or services for students who respond
affected_role: Advisors tutoring counseling financial aid and leadership
severity_rationale: Better detection can increase unmet demand when staffing referral inventory and escalation rules are not aligned
source_context: Reported period (imprecise): current. Products route cases and prioritize students while sector guidance frames interoperability and change management as institutional capabilities
prevalence_limitations: Inference; no reviewed source measures capacity shortfall caused by a specific platform
